title: Clawhammer banjo
summary: Clawhammer, or frailing, is a way of playing the five-string banjo from the Appalachian mountains of the United States. A fingernail strikes down on the melody strings and the short fifth string answers on the off-beat, making the rolling pattern called bum-ditty.
howToPlay: Four strings run up the neck and a short fifth string sits beside the thumb; each lane marks a note, and the Thumb lane is that short string.
A bead slides down toward its place. Strike the note just as the bead lands.
In most tunes a Thumb bead follows each note on the off-beat; pick it right after the downward stroke.
Start with the bum-ditty basics, then try the reel and the slow waltz.
rules: The strings are tuned to an open G chord, with the short fifth string pitched at G above.
A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The Thumb lane is a drone string and sounds on the off-beat in the bum-ditty pattern.
Every tune is played through twice.
heritageNote: The banjo came to North America in the music of enslaved Africans and was shaped by generations of Black and white musicians into the old-time sound of the Appalachian region. Clawhammer playing there accompanies fiddle tunes, ballads and square dances.
